newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end mostly up on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end mostly up on weak yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mostly firmer in lacklustre Tuesday trade, reflecting the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from four to seven yen per gram firmer, with benchmark October finishing up six yen to 1,331 yen.

"Activity was mainly dominated by inter-month trade by trading houses in line with the currency market, while private investors who have held massive long positions in Tokyo gold futures, retreated to the sidelines," a trading house trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was little changed, quoted at $367.90/8.40 per ounce at 0736 GMT, against $367.90/8.30 in New York on Monday.
Sentiment in both the bullion and futures markets remained bearish, traders said.
"The near-term focus is on whether gold will break through initial resistance at $366.00. Gold may head south unless a significant correction occurs in the U.S. stock market," one trader said.
For gold futures, the market is likely to be pressured by long-liquidation ahead of the year-end, the traders said.
